accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the demand for a Constituent Assembly in chronological order:
A. Acceptance of the demand in principle in the August Offer
B. Cabinet Mission scheme
C. Tilak's Swaraj Bill
D. The demand becoming an official Congress demand
accepted.x: Tilak's Swaraj Bill belongs to 1895, the Congress adopted the demand in 1935, the August Offer accepted it in principle in 1940, and the Cabinet Mission scheme followed in 1946.
accepted.tq: Use the dated milestones and identify the first and last events before solving the middle sequence.
accepted.sec: Idea of a Constituent Assembly - first proposer, Congress demand, British acceptance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the Cripps Proposals in relation to the Constituent Assembly?
o: They introduced the Indian Independence Bill in the House of Commons.
They provided for the election of all members by adult franchise.
They carried forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly after its acceptance in principle in the August Offer.
They finally constituted the Assembly through the Cabinet Mission Plan.
accepted.x: The Cripps Proposals of 1942 carried forward the proposal after the British had accepted the demand in principle through the August Offer of 1940. The Assembly was ultimately formed under the Cabinet Mission scheme in 1946.
accepted.tq: Distinguish between an intermediate proposal and the plan that actually constituted the Assembly.
accepted.sec: Idea of a Constituent Assembly - first proposer, Congress demand, British acceptance  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.
2. It came into effect on 15 August 1947.
3. It provided for the creation of two dominions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947, created the two dominions, and took effect on 15 August 1947.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the sequence of assent, provisions and commencement.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 provided that the two new dominions would have the right to:
o: remain permanently under the British Parliament
retain the office of the Viceroy permanently
accepted.x: The Act created two dominions with the right to secede from the Commonwealth. It did not permanently retain British legislative supremacy or the office of the Viceroy.
accepted.tq: Test the precise constitutional status granted to the new dominions rather than a general idea of independence.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: North-West Frontier Province and Sylhet — referendums
accepted.x: Paramountcy lapsed over the princely states under the Indian Independence Act, 1947; it was not continued. Partition votes were held in Punjab and Bengal, while referendums were held in the NWFP and Sylhet.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed provision by distinguishing lapse of paramountcy from its continuation.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Indian Independence Act, 1947, consider the following statements:
1. Paramountcy lapsed over the princely states.
2. Boundary commissions were provided for.
3. The offices of the Viceroy and the Secretary of State continued without change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Act ended the offices of the Viceroy and the Secretary of State, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong institutional statement by checking whether the colonial offices survived the Act.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The period between the introduction of the Indian Independence Bill and the royal assent to it was approximately:
accepted.x: The Bill was introduced on 4 July 1947 and received royal assent on 18 July 1947, a period of about 15 days.
accepted.tq: Calculate the interval from the two dated legislative stages instead of confusing it with the commencement date.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 transformed the Constituent Assembly into:
o: an advisory body subordinate to the Secretary of State
a nominated council of the princely states
only a judicial body for settling boundary disputes
a fully sovereign body and the Dominion Legislature
accepted.x: After the Act, the Constituent Assembly became fully sovereign and also functioned as the Dominion Legislature.
accepted.tq: Match the Act with its institutional consequence for the Constituent Assembly.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The strength of the Constituent Assembly after the withdrawal of the Muslim League members was:
accepted.x: The original strength was 389. After Partition and the withdrawal of the League members, the strength of the Assembly fell to 299.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original total from the post-Partition strength.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Royal assent to the Indian Independence Bill
B. Attlee's declaration regarding British withdrawal
C. Announcement of the Mountbatten Plan
D. Commencement of the two dominions
accepted.x: Attlee's declaration was made on 20 February 1947, the Mountbatten Plan was announced on 3 June, royal assent was given on 18 July, and the dominions came into being on 15 August.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence using the February, June, July and August dates.
accepted.sec: Indian Independence Act 1947 - bill, provisions, dominion status, lapse of paramountcy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission that proposed the scheme for forming the Constituent Assembly consisted of:
o: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander
A.V. Alexander, Rajendra Prasad and Stafford Cripps
accepted.x: The Cabinet Mission consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander. It arrived in India in 1946 to work out the constitutional and political arrangements.
accepted.tq: Use the complete membership combination and reject substitutions by other contemporary figures.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India on:
accepted.x: The Cabinet Mission arrived on 24 March 1946. The other dates relate to later developments connected with British withdrawal and independence.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Cabinet Mission date and the later dates of the transfer of power.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, the total proposed strength of the Constituent Assembly was:
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly was planned to have 389 members: 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.
accepted.tq: Use the total and its two-part division to avoid confusing the figure with the post-Partition strength.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the distribution of the 389 seats under the Cabinet Mission scheme?
o: 296 for British India and 93 for princely states
299 for British India and 90 for princely states
208 for British India and 181 for princely states
293 for British India and 96 for princely states
accepted.x: The scheme allotted 296 seats to British India and 93 seats to the princely states, making a total of 389.
accepted.tq: Split the total into its two component figures before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approximate basis used for allocating seats in the Constituent Assembly was:
o: one seat for every million people
one seat for every five lakh people
one seat for every ten million people
one seat for every one lakh people
accepted.x: The seats were allocated approximately on the basis of one seat for every million people.
accepted.tq: Test the population-to-seat ratio directly and watch the scale of the figures.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the provincial allocation of seats to the Constituent Assembly, the communities specifically recognised were:
accepted.x: Provincial seats were divided among Muslims, Sikhs and the General category according to population.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact three-category classification instead of replacing it with broader community labels.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the princely states' representation in the Constituent Assembly is correct?
o: Their representatives were directly elected by adult citizens.
Their representatives were elected by the Provincial Assemblies.
Their representatives were nominated by the rulers, and the 93 seats were initially unfilled.
Their representatives were selected by the British Parliament.
accepted.x: The rulers nominated the representatives of the princely states. The 93 seats allotted to them remained unfilled at first.
accepted.tq: Combine the authority responsible for nomination with the initial status of the seats.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was partly elected and partly nominated.
2. It was based on adult franchise.
3. Gandhi and Jinnah were not members of the Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Assembly was partly elected and partly nominated, and Gandhi and Jinnah were not members. It was not based on adult franchise, making statement 2 false.
accepted.tq: Spot the single reversed constitutional feature among otherwise correct statements.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 1946 election results for the Constituent Assembly included which of the following combinations?
accepted.x: The 1946 results recorded 208 seats for the Congress, 73 for the Muslim League and 15 for independents.
accepted.tq: Keep the three result figures together and reject options that interchange or alter one component.
accepted.sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, method of election, seats  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who were the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
accepted.x: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari served as the Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two Vice-Presidents from the provisional president, constitutional adviser and legislative chair.
accepted.sec: Key persons - provisional president, president, constitutional adviser, vice-presidents  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Sir B.N. Rau is correct?
o: He chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.
He prepared the initial draft and later served as a judge of the International Court of Justice during 1951–52.
He was the provisional president as the eldest member.
He chaired the Assembly in its capacity as the Dominion Legislature.
accepted.x: B.N. Rau prepared the initial draft and later served as a judge of the International Court of Justice in 1951–52. The other offices were held by different persons.
accepted.tq: Match the person with both the constitutional role and the later international office.
accepted.sec: Key persons - provisional president, president, constitutional adviser, vice-presidents  [other exams]

accepted.s: When the Constituent Assembly functioned as the Dominion Legislature, it was chaired by:
accepted.x: G.V. Mavalankar chaired the Constituent Assembly when it functioned as the Dominion Legislature.
accepted.tq: Separate the Assembly's constitutional role from its legislative role and identify the corresponding chair.
accepted.sec: Key persons - provisional president, president, constitutional adviser, vice-presidents  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Drafting Committee is correctly matched?
o: N. Madhava Rau — replaced B.L. Mitter
T.T. Krishnamachari — replaced N. Madhava Rau
accepted.x: N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter in the Drafting Committee. T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan.
accepted.tq: Track the replacement pairs carefully; APPSC commonly swaps the incoming and outgoing names.
accepted.sec: Key persons - provisional president, president, constitutional adviser, vice-presidents  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
accepted.x: H.C. Mukherjee was a Vice-President of the Constituent Assembly, not a member of the Drafting Committee. N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Syed Mohammad Saadullah and K.M. Munshi were members.
accepted.tq: Use office-based elimination to find the person belonging to a neighbouring constitutional position.
accepted.sec: Key persons - provisional president, president, constitutional adviser, vice-presidents  [other exams]

accepted.s: The original Preamble of the Constitution was illuminated by:
accepted.x: The original Preamble was illuminated by Beohar Rammanohar Sinha. This is distinct from the persons associated with handwriting or other artwork in the original Constitution.
accepted.tq: Apply confusable-person discrimination among artists and contributors associated with the original Constitution.
accepted.sec: Key persons - provisional president, president, constitutional adviser, vice-presidents  [other exams]
